prompt.adult: Others reported how the Thessalonians turned to God to serve the living and true God. From what did they turn, according to 1:9?
prompt.child: People everywhere heard how the Thessalonians changed. What did they turn away from to serve God?
prompt.teen: 1 Thessalonians 1:9: “how you turned to God” from what?
prompt.older: According to 1 Thessalonians 1:9, from what did the Thessalonians turn to God?

verses.text: For they themselves declare concerning us what manner of entry we had to you, and how you turned to God from idols to serve the living and true God,

explanation.child: Look right after “turned to God” in verse 9.
explanation.teen: 1:9 tells what others declare about Paul’s visit, then what the Thessalonians turned from and to. Read the middle.
explanation.older: It follows “how you turned to God” in 1:9.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:9 says they turned to serve the living and true God. 1:10 says they wait for His Son from heaven.
teaching.takeaway: They turned to God from idols.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 2:7 Paul says they were gentle among the Thessalonians. To whom does he compare that gentleness?
prompt.child: Paul says he was gentle with the believers in Thessalonica. Who does he compare himself to?
prompt.teen: 1 Thessalonians 2:7: “But we were gentle among you, just as” who?
prompt.older: According to 1 Thessalonians 2:7, whom were Paul and his companions like in their gentleness?

verses.text: But we were gentle among you, just as a nursing mother cherishes her own children.

explanation.child: Look at the words right after “just as” in verse 7.
explanation.teen: 2:6 says they could have made demands; 2:7 says they were gentle, then gives a picture. Read the picture.
explanation.older: It follows “gentle among you, just as” in 2:7.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:6 says they might have made demands as apostles of Christ. 2:8 says they were well pleased to impart their own lives.
teaching.takeaway: They were gentle, just as a nursing mother cherishes her own children.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 2:17 Paul says they longed to see the Thessalonians’ face with great desire. According to 2:18, why had he not come, time and again?
prompt.child: Paul really wanted to visit the believers in Thessalonica again. What does 2:18 say stopped him?
prompt.teen: 1 Thessalonians 2:18: “Therefore we wanted to come to you—even I, Paul, time and again—but” what?
prompt.older: According to 1 Thessalonians 2:18, what kept Paul from coming to them?

verses.text: But we, brethren, having been taken away from you for a short time in presence, not in heart, endeavored more eagerly to see your face with great desire.
Therefore we wanted to come to you—even I, Paul, time and again—but Satan hindered us.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 18.
explanation.teen: 2:17 tells of their longing; 2:18 says they wanted to come, names Paul, and then says what happened. Read the end.

teaching.extended_explanation: 2:17 says they were taken away from them for a short time, in presence, not in heart. 2:19 asks what is their hope, or joy.
teaching.takeaway: Paul wanted to come, but “Satan hindered us.”

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 3:9 Paul asks what thanks he can render to God for all his joy over them. According to 3:10, he prays night and day to see their face and to do what?
prompt.child: Paul thanked God for the believers and prayed day and night to see them again. What else did he want to do for their faith?
prompt.teen: 1 Thessalonians 3:10: “night and day praying exceedingly that we may see your face and” what?
prompt.older: According to 1 Thessalonians 3:10, what did Paul pray to do, besides seeing their face?

verses.text: For what thanks can we render to God for you, for all the joy with which we rejoice for your sake before our God,
night and day praying exceedingly that we may see your face and perfect what is lacking in your faith?

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 10.
explanation.teen: 3:9 asks a question about thanks; 3:10 says how Paul prays and for two things. Read the second.
explanation.older: It follows “that we may see your face and” in 3:10.

teaching.extended_explanation: 3:6 says Timothy brought good news of their faith and love. 3:9 speaks of all the joy with which Paul rejoices for their sake.
teaching.takeaway: He prayed to see them and perfect what is lacking in their faith.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: 4:14 says God will bring with Him those who sleep in Jesus. In 4:13, Paul does not want them to sorrow as whom?
prompt.child: Paul writes to comfort believers whose loved ones had died. According to 4:13, he does not want them to be sad like whom?
prompt.older: Read with 4:14, like whom should believers not sorrow, according to 4:13?

verses.text: But I do not want you to be ignorant, brethren, concerning those who have fallen asleep, lest you sorrow as others who have no hope.
For if we believe that Jesus died and rose again, even so God will bring with Him those who sleep in Jesus.

explanation.child: Look at the last words of verse 13.
explanation.teen: 4:13 names those who have fallen asleep, then says how not to sorrow. 4:14 gives the reason. Read the end of 4:13.
explanation.older: It follows “lest you sorrow as” in 4:13.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:14 says Jesus died and rose again. 4:18 says to comfort one another with these words.
teaching.takeaway: Do not sorrow as others who have no hope.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: In 3:12 Paul prays that the Lord make them abound in love to one another. In 4:9, why does he not need to write to them about brotherly love?
prompt.child: Paul prayed for the believers to love each other more. Later, why did he say he did not need to write to them about loving each other?
prompt.older: Read with 3:12, what reason does 4:9 give that Paul need not write about brotherly love?

verses.text: And may the Lord make you increase and abound in love to one another and to all, just as we do to you,
But concerning brotherly love you have no need that I should write to you, for you yourselves are taught by God to love one another;

explanation.adult: Read the words after “you yourselves are” in 4:9.
explanation.child: Look right after “you yourselves are” in verse 9.
explanation.teen: 3:12 is a prayer about love; 4:9 says there is no need to write, then gives a reason. Read the reason.
explanation.older: It follows “for you yourselves are” in 4:9.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:10 says they love all the brethren in all Macedonia. 3:12 prays they would abound in love to all.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: 1:10 says Jesus delivers us from the wrath to come. According to 5:9, what did God appoint us to, instead of wrath?
prompt.child: Paul says Jesus rescues believers from God’s anger to come. What does 5:9 say God chose believers for instead?
prompt.teen: 1 Thessalonians 5:9: “For God did not appoint us to wrath, but” to what?
prompt.older: Beside 1:10, what does 5:9 say God appointed us for?

verses.text: and to wait for His Son from heaven, whom He raised from the dead, even Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come.
For God did not appoint us to wrath, but to obtain salvation through our Lord Jesus Christ,

explanation.child: Look right after “to wrath, but” in verse 9.
explanation.teen: 1:10 speaks of waiting for His Son; 5:9 says what God did not appoint us to, then what He did, and through whom. Read the middle.
explanation.older: It follows “did not appoint us to wrath, but” in 5:9.

teaching.extended_explanation: 1:10 says they wait for His Son from heaven, whom He raised from the dead. 5:10 says He died for us.
teaching.takeaway: God appointed us to obtain salvation through our Lord.

review.notes: Fruitful stage. NKJV excerpt copied from _fruitful_nkjv.json (BibleGateway NKJV). Answer is in the cited verse.

prompt.adult: 2:12 urges them to walk worthy of God, who calls them into His own kingdom and glory. In 4:12, how should they walk toward those who are outside?
prompt.child: Paul tells believers to live in a way that honors God. In 4:12, how should they live toward people outside the church?
prompt.teen: 1 Thessalonians 4:12: “that you may walk” how “toward those who are outside”?
prompt.older: Beside 2:12, how does 4:12 say they should walk toward outsiders?

verses.text: that you would walk worthy of God who calls you into His own kingdom and glory.
that you may walk properly toward those who are outside, and that you may lack nothing.

explanation.teen: 2:12 speaks of walking worthy; 4:12 says how to walk toward outsiders, then that you may lack nothing. Read the first part.
explanation.older: It follows “that you may walk” in 4:12.

teaching.extended_explanation: 4:11 urges them to lead a quiet life and work with their own hands. 4:12 adds that they may lack nothing.
teaching.takeaway: They should walk properly toward those who are outside.
